Humphrey]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Bob Smith (New Hampshire politician)|Bob Smith]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in New Hampshire}} The '''1990 United States Senate election in New Hampshire''' was held on November 6, 1990. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] U.S. Senator [[Gordon J. Humphrey]] decided to retire and not run for re-election to a third term. Republican [[Bob Smith (New Hampshire politician)|Bob Smith]] won the open seat, easily defeating the Democratic nominee, former senator [[John A. Durkin]]. == Republican primary == ===Candidates=== * [[Thomas K. Elsnau (Libertarian) * [[Bob Smith (New Hampshire politician)|Bob Smith]], U.S. Representative from [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire|Wolfeboro]] (Republican) ===Campaign=== The 1990 New Hampshire Senate race garnered national news after John Durkin, previously a senator from New Hampshire in 1975–1980, made a remark that was perceived as a racial slur against the Japanese. Durkin told reporters interviewing him, "If you want a Jap in the United States Senate, then vote for Bob Smith". "Jap" is a term that was frequently used in WWII to describe the Japanese, and was, by 1990, considered racist terminology. The quote destroyed Durkin's campaign and he ended up losing to Smith by a more than 2-to-1 margin, a devastating blow for the ex-Senator.{{cite web |last1=Leubsdorf |first1=Ben |title=Former U.S. Senator John Durkin dies |url=https://www.concordmonitor.com/Archive/2012/10/999638361-999638362-14-CM |website=Concord Monitor |publisher=CM |access-date=16 May 2019 |archive-date=August 30, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200830174051/https://www.concordmonitor.com/Archive/2012/10/999638361-999638362-14-CM |url-status=live }} ===Results=== {{Election box begin | title = 1990 U.S. Senate election in New Hampshire{{Cite web|url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=3533|title=Our Campaigns - NH US Senate Race - Nov 06, 1990|access-date=April 23, 2009|archive-date=June 15, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110615101406/http://www.ourcampaigns.com/RaceDetail.html?RaceID=3533|url-status=live}}}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link | party = Republican Party (United States) | candidate = Bob Smith | votes = 189,792 | percentage = 65.13% | change = }} {{Election box candidate with party link | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = John A.
